robot.name: Xiaomi CyberOne
robot.status_notes: Unveiled on 2022-08-11 as a technology demonstrator and never offered for sale. No runtime, autonomy or customer deployment evidence was found. A 2026 YouTube title references a 'CyberOne V2' at WRC 2026, but no primary successor documentation was available in the reviewed sources, so the original is treated as superseded.
intended_use_cases: future manufacturing and companion-robot exploration (stated aspiration, not deployment)

height.notes: Technobaboy, robotsusa and Inceptive Mind report 177 cm. Manufacturing Today says 5.9 feet, a minor conflict. No Xiaomi official spec page was in the reviewed sources.

weight.notes: Manufacturing Today reports 115 pounds, about 52 kg.

payload.original_value: 6 pounds total; 3 pounds per hand; 1.5 kg per hand
payload.notes: Manufacturing Today reports 6 lb total and 3 lb per hand; robotsusa and Inceptive Mind report 1.5 kg per hand. The catalog uses 6 lb as total payload. Values conflict; 2.72 kg is the converted 6 lb total.

runtime.notes: No runtime or battery duration was disclosed in reviewed sources.

battery.notes: Battery capacity and chemistry were not disclosed in reviewed sources.

walking_speed.notes: robotsusa reports about 3.6 km/h, equivalent to 1.0 m/s. No independent gait measurement.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Technobaboy, robotsusa and Inceptive Mind report 21 DoF across 13 joints; hand DoF was not disclosed.

hands.description: Each hand is reported to hold up to 1.5 kg; upper-limb actuators deliver up to 30 Nm. No finger or hand degrees of freedom, tactile sensing or dexterity specification was disclosed.

items: Mi-Sense depth vision module (reported by robotsusa)
pair of microphones reported to identify 85 environmental sound types and 45 human emotion classifications

compute.description: Not disclosed. Lei Jun is quoted saying AI and mechanical capabilities are self-developed by Xiaomi Robotics Lab, but no onboard compute, chip or model details were provided.

actuators.description: 13 joints and 21 DoF reported; 0.5 ms per-DoF response; upper-limb motor about 500 g with up to 30 Nm; peak hip torque up to 300 Nm.

availability.notes: Xiaomi did not announce commercial sales. Lei Jun reportedly estimated 600,000-700,000 yuan when it goes on sale, and a third-party reseller lists $99,999, but neither is an official sale price. No sale date was found.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Reported single-hand payload of 1.5 kg and programming by demonstration; the launch stage appearance included handing a flower to Lei Jun. No finger-level dexterity, grasp taxonomy or manipulation benchmark was published.
caveats: Payload and stage gesture only; no independent manipulation testing.
Hand degrees of freedom and tactile sensing were not disclosed.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: No autonomous task execution was documented in the reviewed sources. Inceptive Mind described CyberOne as mostly a prototype that did not seem able to perform many practical tasks. A 2026 YouTube title says 'Completely Alone' for a CyberOne V2 florist demo, but no transcript or description was available, so autonomy is not credited.
caveats: No autonomous task video with disclosed execution mode.
YouTube title alone cannot establish autonomy.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Reported 21 DoF across 13 joints, 0.5 ms per-DoF response, 300 Nm peak hip torque and about 3.6 km/h walking; media reported it walked onstage and handed over a flower. No independent gait, balance-recovery or fall-rate data.
caveats: Launch-stage demonstration only; no measured gait metrics.
Runtime and terrain capability were not disclosed.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Reported Mi-Sense depth vision, 3D reconstruction, and recognition of 85 environmental sound types and 45 human emotion classifications. These are company/media claims without a published benchmark.
caveats: No accuracy, latency or independent perception benchmark.

human_interaction.summary: Curved OLED face display, microphones for sound/emotion classification, and a launch-stage interaction in which CyberOne greeted Lei Jun and handed him a flower. No measured conversational or emotion-recognition reliability.
caveats: Stage script and teleoperation status were not disclosed.
No user study or interaction benchmark.

endurance_reliability.summary: No runtime, battery capacity, duty cycle, MTBF or endurance test was disclosed in the reviewed sources.
caveats: Cannot assess reliability from a launch demonstrator.

human_environment_fit.summary: Human-scale at 177 cm and 52 kg with a face display, but no safety certification, runtime or home/factory operating data was found. Never sold.
caveats: No safety or human-proximity testing published.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: No customer deployment, pilot or commercial sale was found. Xiaomi did not announce commercial sales; a 2024 blog's factory-floor claims are unsourced, and a 2026 YouTube title about an EV factory has no transcript.
caveats: Factory and elder-care claims are speculative or title-only.
No units, hours or output metrics.

accessibility_value.summary: Never offered for sale; no official price, lease, waitlist or purchase channel. Reported expected cost of 600,000-700,000 yuan and a third-party $99,999 listing do not establish accessibility.
caveats: Expected cost is far above consumer accessibility.

evidence_items.title: IEEE Spectrum CyberOne article title (body unavailable)
evidence_items.claim: IEEE Spectrum published an article titled 'Xiaomi Builds a Humanoid Robot for Some Reason'; the supplied page text contained only the title, navigation and comments, so no specifications were taken from it.
evidence_items.notes: Article body was not present in the supplied source text.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Establishes independent media coverage but not technical facts.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Xiaomi Builds a Humanoid Robot for Some Reason
evidence_items.verification_notes: Do not use for specs; the article body was unavailable.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne launch dimensions
evidence_items.claim: CyberOne is reported at 177 cm tall, 52 kg, with a 168 cm arm span.
evidence_items.notes: Secondary report of the Xiaomi launch.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: CyberOne is a humanoid robot measuring 177cm in height and 52kg by weight, with an arm span of 168cm.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No Xiaomi official spec page in the pack; consistent with robotsusa and Inceptive Mind.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne 21 DoF and 0.5 ms response
evidence_items.claim: CyberOne is reported to support 21 degrees of freedom with 0.5 ms response per degree of freedom.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: It supports up to 21 degrees of freedom in motion and achieves a real-time response speed of 0.5ms for each degree of freedom, which allows it to fully simulate human movements.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne peak torque and posture balancing
evidence_items.claim: CyberOne is reported to use bipedal-motion posture balancing with peak torque up to 300 Nm.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: To stay upright, CyberOne is fitted with advanced arms and legs that supports bipedal-motion posture balancing with a peak torque of up to 300Nm.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne emotion and vision claims
evidence_items.claim: CyberOne is reported to detect human emotion, use advanced vision and create three-dimensional virtual reconstructions of the real world.
evidence_items.notes: Launch claim relayed by media; no accuracy data.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Basis for interaction and scene-understanding claims.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: It also has the ability to detect human emotion, and features advanced vision capabilities and functionality that allows it to create three-dimensional virtual reconstructions of the real world, alongside a host of other advanced technologies.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne appears onstage with Lei Jun
evidence_items.claim: At the Beijing launch, CyberOne joined Lei Jun onstage, greeted him and handed him a long-stem flower.
evidence_items.notes: Live stage appearance reported by media; video not reviewed.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Only public interaction demo found for this robot.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The humanoid robot was unveiled at a launch event in Beijing, where the bipedal humanoid robot joined Lei Jun onstage, greeting the CEO and handing him a long-stem flower.
evidence_items.source_location: Inceptive Mind article body, launch description
evidence_items.verification_notes: Stage actions may be scripted; execution mode not disclosed.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne described as mostly a prototype
evidence_items.claim: Inceptive Mind characterized CyberOne as mostly a prototype that did not seem able to perform many practical tasks.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: At the moment, CyberOne should probably be seen mostly as a prototype that so far does not seem to be able to perform many practical tasks.
evidence_items.source_location: Inceptive Mind article body, assessment paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: Consistent with the absence of deployment evidence.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne single-hand payload and demonstration
evidence_items.claim: CyberOne is reported to hold up to 1.5 kg in one hand and to support programming by demonstration.
evidence_items.notes: Payload is not equivalent to dexterous manipulation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: In addition, CyberOne can hold up to 1.5kg in weight with a single hand and programming by demonstration.
evidence_items.source_location: Inceptive Mind article body, upper-limb paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: No hand DoF or grasp-quality data.

evidence_items.title: CyberOne expected cost and no sale date
evidence_items.claim: Lei Jun reportedly estimated 600,000-700,000 yuan when CyberOne goes on sale; no sale date was given.
evidence_items.notes: Expected future price, not an official sale price.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Lei Jun stated that CyberOne would cost somewhere in the range of 600,000 to 700,000 yuan (about $89,100 to $104,000) when it goes on sale.
evidence_items.source_location: Inceptive Mind article body, pricing paragraph
evidence_items.verification_notes: No Xiaomi sales page or date.

evidence_items.title: Secondary specification listing for CyberOne
evidence_items.claim: A reseller/directory listing reports 177 cm, 52 kg, 168 cm arm span, 21 DoF across 13 joints and 0.5 ms joint response.
evidence_items.notes: Third-party listing, not Xiaomi official documentation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: It stands 177 cm tall, weighs 52 kg, and has a 168 cm arm span, with 21 degrees of freedom across 13 joints and a 0.5 ms joint response time.
evidence_items.source_location: robotsusa.com product page, overview and technical section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Reseller page; use only as secondary corroboration.

evidence_items.title: Secondary listing: walking speed and perception
evidence_items.claim: A reseller/directory listing reports Mi-Sense depth vision, 45 emotion classifications, 85 environmental sound types, a curved OLED face and walking speed around 3.6 km/h.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supports speed and perception claims weakly.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The platform combines a Mi-Sense depth vision module, recognition of 45 human emotion classifications from voice and 85 environmental sound types, a curved OLED face display, and bipedal posture balancing with a walking speed of around 3.6 km/h.
evidence_items.source_location: robotsusa.com product page, overview and perception sections

evidence_items.title: Secondary listing: per-hand payload
evidence_items.claim: A reseller/directory listing reports each hand can hold up to 1.5 kg.
evidence_items.notes: Conflicts with Manufacturing Today's 3 lb per hand.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Each hand can additionally hold up to 1.5 kg, letting the robot carry small objects while it moves.
evidence_items.source_location: robotsusa.com product page, walking and balancing section

evidence_items.title: No commercial sales announced
evidence_items.claim: Xiaomi presented CyberOne as a research and ecosystem exploration platform and did not announce commercial sales; cost figures were manufacturing estimates rather than a list price.
evidence_items.notes: Secondary listing explicitly says no commercial sales.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Xiaomi presented CyberOne as a research and ecosystem exploration platform, and the company did not announce commercial sales; cost figures mentioned around the unveiling referred to manufacturing estimates rather than a list price.
evidence_items.source_location: robotsusa.com product page, pricing and availability section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Consistent with Inceptive Mind's no-sale-date report.

evidence_items.title: Conflicting payload and joint count
evidence_items.claim: Manufacturing Today reports a 6 lb total lift, 3 lb per hand and 13 joints, conflicting with the 1.5 kg per hand reports.
evidence_items.notes: Low-confidence secondary article with unsourced figures.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The robot can lift up to 6 pounds, with a maximum of 3 pounds in each hand, thanks to its system of 13 joints that provide flexibility and strength.
evidence_items.source_location: Manufacturing Today article body, features section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Payload conflicts with 1.5 kg per hand claims; treat as low confidence.

evidence_items.title: Unsourced factory-efficiency claim
evidence_items.claim: A 2024 blog claims a future 15-20% efficiency increase and factory integration for CyberOne without citing primary evidence.
evidence_items.notes: Speculative blog; no customer, site, hours or output data.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Should not be credited as deployment evidence.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Internal estimates suggest a future potential 15-20% increase in efficiency for specific tasks.
evidence_items.source_location: The bLife Movement article, manufacturing section
evidence_items.verification_notes: No primary source or named deployment.

evidence_items.title: Missing runtime, battery, compute and hand DoF
evidence_items.claim: No runtime, battery capacity, onboard compute, hand degrees of freedom or independent test result was disclosed in the reviewed sources.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should not infer missing specs from directories.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure is not evidence of inability.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No Xiaomi official product page, manual or technical paper was present in the reviewed sources; most specifications come from secondary reports and a reseller listing.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Specs should be treated as reported, not manufacturer-verified.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No runtime, battery capacity, charging method or duty cycle was disclosed.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Endurance and reliability cannot be scored above minimal evidence.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: No autonomous task execution with disclosed execution mode was found; the 2026 florist YouTube title has no transcript.
No customer, site, hours, units or output metrics found. The 2024 factory blog and 2026 EV-factory YouTube title provide no verifiable deployment evidence.
Manufacturing Today reports 6 lb total and 3 lb per hand; robotsusa and Inceptive Mind report 1.5 kg per hand. The catalog uses 6 lb as total payload.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Use payload cautiously; do not treat as dexterity evidence.

limitations_and_unknowns.description: YouTube sources 7-11 were available only as titles and channel/date metadata, with no transcripts or visual review.
limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Cannot support hand-upgrade, sweating-cooling, V2 florist or factory claims.

limitations_and_unknowns.impact_on_arena_scoring: Keep human-interaction and safety confidence low.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Compiled automatically from public sources on 2026-10-30 and needs human review. CyberOne is a 2022 technology demonstrator with secondary reporting of human-scale specs and a stage interaction, but no official documentation, runtime, autonomy, customer deployment or sale path. The 2026 successor/video titles cannot be credited without transcripts or primary sources.
strongest_positive_evidence: Multiple secondary sources report 177 cm height, 52 kg weight, 21 DoF across 13 joints and 0.5 ms response.
Reported peak hip torque up to 300 Nm, about 3.6 km/h walking and 1.5 kg per hand.
Media-reported launch-stage interaction in which CyberOne greeted Lei Jun and handed him a flower.
Reported Mi-Sense depth vision and 45 emotion / 85 sound recognition claims.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No Xiaomi official product page, manual or technical paper in the reviewed sources.
No runtime, battery capacity, onboard compute or hand DoF.
No autonomous task execution, customer deployment or independent benchmark.
2026 hand-upgrade, sweating, V2 florist and EV-factory evidence is title-only YouTube material.
conflicting_claims: Height: 177 cm (Technobaboy, robotsusa, Inceptive Mind) vs 5.9 feet (Manufacturing Today).
Payload: 6 lb total / 3 lb per hand (Manufacturing Today) vs 1.5 kg per hand (robotsusa, Inceptive Mind).
Price: 600,000-700,000 yuan expected (Inceptive Mind) vs $89,000-$104,000 (Manufacturing Today) vs $99,999 reseller listing (robotsusa).
Joint wording: 21 DoF across 13 joints in several sources; Manufacturing Today mentions 13 joints without clarifying DoF.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit factory deployment or the 15-20% efficiency claim from a 2024 blog.
Do not credit the YouTube 'Completely Alone' florist title as autonomous execution.
Do not credit hand-upgrade or sweating-cooling claims from title-only YouTube sources.
Do not treat the $99,999 reseller listing as an official Xiaomi price.
Do not describe CyberOne as purchasable or commercially deployed.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Xiaomi CyberOne is a 2022 full-size biped demonstrator reported at 177 cm, 52 kg, 21 DoF across 13 joints, about 3.6 km/h and up to 300 Nm hip torque, with a curved OLED face, Mi-Sense depth vision and claimed recognition of 45 emotion classifications and 85 environmental sounds. Media reported it appearing onstage with Lei Jun and handing him a flower. Xiaomi did not announce commercial sales; no runtime, battery, onboard compute, hand DoF, autonomous task execution, customer deployment or independent test was found. Later factory, hand-upgrade and V2 florist claims are either unsourced or available only as YouTube titles without transcripts.
strongest_evidence: Multiple secondary sources report 177 cm, 52 kg, 21 DoF across 13 joints and 0.5 ms response.
Reported 1.5 kg per hand and up to 300 Nm peak hip torque.
Media-reported launch-stage interaction with Lei Jun.
weakest_evidence: No Xiaomi official product page or manual in the reviewed sources.
No runtime, battery, onboard compute or hand DoF.
No autonomous task, customer deployment or independent benchmark.
known_do_not_credit: Factory deployment or 15-20% efficiency gains from a 2024 blog.
Autonomous florist demonstration from a YouTube title.
Hand upgrade or sweating-cooling claims from YouTube titles.
$99,999 reseller listing as an official price.
